title: Secret scanning of a repo and key rotation
when: Code or history may hold committed API keys, passwords or private keys, or a secret already leaked, and every copy must be found, rotated and blocked from coming back.
inputs: issuers of the keys in use
prompt:
Goal: A list of every exposed secret with its location, each one rotated at its issuer, and a local check that blocks new ones.
Steps:
1. Scan the working tree with patterns: -----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----, AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}, (api[_-]?key|secret|token|passw(or)?d)\s*[:=]\s*["'][^"']{12,}, and long hex or base64 values in config files.
2. Scan history too: git log -p --all -S "<prefix>" or git grep -E "<pattern>" $(git rev-list --all); a value in any old commit counts as exposed.
3. Also look in .env files, logs, fixtures, notebooks, build output and CI files.
4. Per hit record file and line or commit, kind, issuer and whether it is live; show only the first 4 characters.
5. Rotate: issue a new secret, deploy it through config, confirm it works, revoke the old one, read the issuer access logs.
6. Prevent: values move to environment or secret files, .env goes in .gitignore, and scripts/scan-secrets.mjs runs from a pre-commit hook.
Quality bar:
- History rewriting is optional cleanup, never a stand in for rotation.
- Live and privileged secrets come first.
- The hook runs offline.
Pitfalls:
- Deleting the file in a new commit and calling it fixed.
- Pasting the secret into tickets or chat.
- Revoking before the replacement is live, causing an outage.
Verify:
- [ ] Tree and history were both scanned.
- [ ] Each live secret has a rotation status.
- [ ] No full secret value is in the report.
- [ ] The hook fails on a planted fake key.
Output: SECRETS-REPORT.md with findings and rotation status, plus scripts/scan-secrets.mjs.

examples.input: acho que commitei uma chave da API no repositorio
examples.output: tree and history scan, masked findings table, rotate then revoke plan, pre-commit scanner script
